issues.description: PaymentDetails interface stores highly sensitive PCI-DSS data (cardNumber, CVV) in plain text. This violates PCI compliance and creates a massive security risk.
issues.suggestion: Never store or handle raw card data in your application. Use a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, PayPal) that provides tokenization. Replace PaymentDetails with: { paymentToken: string; amount: number }. The payment processor handles card validation and charging.

issues.description: processPremiumPayment function handles raw credit card data (cardNumber, CVV, expiryDate) directly in application code, violating PCI-DSS compliance standards.
issues.suggestion: Remove all direct card handling. Integrate with a payment processor: const result = await paymentGateway.charge({ token: payment.paymentToken, amount }). Card data should only be submitted client-side directly to the payment processor, never through your backend.

issues.description: validatePaymentDetails performs client-side card validation patterns. This suggests card data flows through the application, which is a PCI compliance violation.
issues.suggestion: Remove this function entirely. Payment validation must be done by the payment processor (Stripe, Square, etc.). Your app should only handle opaque payment tokens, never raw card data.

issues.description: chargeCard function logs full payment object to console, potentially exposing card numbers, CVV, and sensitive data in production logs.
issues.suggestion: Remove console.error with payment data. Use structured logging with sanitization: logger.error('Payment failed', { userId, amount, lastFour: payment.cardNumber.slice(-4), error: error.message }). Never log full payment objects.

issues.description: Card number validation checks for exactly 16 digits, but valid cards can be 13-19 digits (Amex=15, Visa=13-16, Mastercard=16, etc.).
issues.suggestion: This validation is insufficient and incorrect. Use a payment processor that handles card validation properly. If you must validate client-side before tokenization, use a library like 'card-validator' or implement Luhn algorithm for all card types.

issues.description: Date expiry validation uses '2000 + parseInt(year)' which will break in 2100 and doesn't handle current month correctly (should check month too).
issues.suggestion: Fix date comparison: const now = new Date(); const expiry = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month)); if (expiry < now) return false; Better yet, remove this entirely and use payment processor validation.

issues.description: chargeCard stores last 4 digits of card but doesn't implement any fraud detection, rate limiting, or idempotency checks. Multiple charges could occur.
issues.suggestion: Implement idempotency: Accept a unique paymentId parameter and check 'SELECT id FROM payments WHERE payment_id = $1' before charging. Add rate limiting middleware. Use a proper payment gateway with built-in fraud detection.

issues.description: chargeCard simulates payment processing with db.query but never actually charges a card. This creates a financial loss vulnerability - users get subscriptions without payment.
issues.suggestion: Integrate real payment processor: const charge = await stripe.charges.create({ amount: amount * 100, currency: 'usd', source: paymentToken }); Only upgrade subscription after confirmed payment.

issues.description: processPremiumPayment has no transaction handling. If chargeCard succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription fails, user is charged without receiving subscription.
issues.suggestion: Wrap in database transaction: const client = await db.getClient(); try { await client.query('BEGIN'); await chargeCard(...); await upgradeUserSubscription(...); await client.query('COMMIT'); } catch(e) { await client.query('ROLLBACK'); throw e; } finally { client.release(); }

issues.description: processPremiumPayment has no idempotency protection. If called twice (network retry, user double-click), user gets charged multiple times.
issues.suggestion: Add idempotency key parameter: processPremiumPayment(userId, payment, tier, idempotencyKey). Check if payment with that key exists before processing: 'SELECT id FROM payments WHERE idempotency_key = $1'. Return existing result if found.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess uses JSON.parse on user-controlled data without error handling. Malformed JSON in database will crash the application.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return features.includes(feature); } catch (e) { logger.error('Invalid features JSON', { userId, error: e }); return false; }

issues.description: calculateSubscriptionPrice has hardcoded tax rate (0.08) and processing fee (0.029). These vary by location/processor and should be configurable.
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration: const config = { taxRate: process.env.TAX_RATE || 0.08, processingFee: 0.029 }; Or pass as parameters: calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier, taxRate, processingFee). Consider using a tax calculation service for multi-region support.

issues.description: calculateSubscriptionPrice returns floating-point result which can cause rounding errors in financial calculations (e.g., 10.77499999999).
issues.suggestion: Use integer cents for all money calculations: return Math.round((basePrice + tax + fee) * 100); Store amounts as cents in database. Convert to dollars only for display: (amount / 100).toFixed(2)

issues.description: upgradeUserSubscription has hardcoded feature lists in conditional logic. Adding new tiers or features requires code changes.
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration object: const TIER_FEATURES = { free: [], premium: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'], enterprise: [...premium, 'api_access', 'team_collaboration'] }; const features = TIER_FEATURES[tier];

issues.description: upgradeUserSubscription sets expiry to exactly 1 year from now, but doesn't account for existing subscription time. User loses remaining days when upgrading.
issues.suggestion: Preserve existing time: const current = await getUserSubscription(userId); const validUntil = current ? new Date(Math.max(current.validUntil.getTime(), Date.now()) + 365*24*60*60*1000) : new Date(Date.now() + 365*24*60*60*1000);

issues.description: upgradeUserSubscription uses INSERT...ON CONFLICT with large query, but doesn't use a prepared statement. Features are JSON-stringified on every call.
issues.suggestion: Use prepared statements for performance: const stmt = await db.prepare('INSERT INTO subscriptions...'); await stmt.run([userId, tier, validUntil, features]); Consider storing features in a separate junction table instead of JSON for better queryability.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess performs SELECT query on every feature check. High-traffic apps will hammer the database unnecessarily.
issues.suggestion: Implement caching with TTL: const cached = await redis.get(`sub:${userId}`); if (cached) return JSON.parse(cached).features.includes(feature); const sub = await getUserSubscription(userId); await redis.setex(`sub:${userId}`, 3600, JSON.stringify(sub)); return sub?.features.includes(feature);

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess checks if validUntil < new Date(), but doesn't handle timezone issues. Could fail at midnight in different timezones.
issues.suggestion: Use UTC timestamps consistently: const validUntil = new Date(subscription.valid_until); const now = new Date(); if (validUntil.getTime() < now.getTime()) return false; Store dates in UTC in database.

issues.description: getUserSubscription uses JSON.parse without error handling. Corrupted database data will throw unhandled exceptions.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: try { return { userId: row.user_id, tier: row.tier, validUntil: new Date(row.valid_until), features: JSON.parse(row.features) }; } catch (e) { logger.error('Invalid subscription data', { userId, error: e }); return null; }

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess duplicates subscription retrieval logic from getUserSubscription. Code duplication increases maintenance burden.
issues.suggestion: Reuse existing function: const subscription = await getUserSubscription(userId); if (!subscription) return false; if (subscription.validUntil < new Date()) return false; return subscription.features.includes(feature);

issues.description: processPremiumPayment accepts payment.amount from client but then calculates its own amount. This creates confusion and potential for exploitation if amounts don't match.
issues.suggestion: Remove amount from PaymentDetails interface (once using tokens). Calculate server-side only: const amount = calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier); if (payment.declaredAmount !== amount) throw new Error('Amount mismatch'); Or don't accept client amount at all.

issues.description: processPremiumPayment has no logging of successful payments, making audit trails and debugging difficult.
issues.suggestion: Add structured logging: logger.info('Payment processed', { userId, tier, amount, paymentId, timestamp: new Date() }); Log at key steps: payment initiated, validated, charged, subscription upgraded.

issues.description: processPremiumPayment returns boolean for success/failure, but throws errors for validation. Inconsistent error handling makes API confusing.
issues.suggestion: Be consistent: Either throw errors for all failures: throw new PaymentFailedError('Card declined'), or return Result<boolean, Error>: return { success: false, error: 'Card declined' }. Throwing is generally better for exceptional cases.

issues.description: Database queries use parameterized queries ($1, $2) which is good, but there's no mention of connection pooling or query timeout limits.
issues.suggestion: Ensure db.query has timeout: await db.query(query, params, { timeout: 5000 }); Use connection pooling with max connections limit. Add query monitoring to detect slow queries.

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUES: This file has severe PCI-DSS compliance violations by handling raw credit card data (cardNumber, CVV) in application code. This is illegal in production and exposes the company to massive liability. The payment processing is also simulated (not real), creating financial loss risk. Additionally, there are multiple high-severity bugs: no transaction handling (users can be charged without getting subscription), no idempotency (double-charging risk), broken expiry date validation, missing error handling on JSON parsing, and no fraud detection. The code also has maintainability issues with hardcoded values, code duplication, and floating-point money calculations. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED before production deployment.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Payment validation is the first line of defense against fraudulent transactions. Weak validation could allow invalid card data to reach payment processors, resulting in security breaches or PCI compliance violations.
Card number validation is essential for PCI compliance and fraud prevention. Accepting invalid card numbers could expose the system to attacks or processing failures.
CVV validation protects against card-not-present fraud. Accepting invalid CVV could result in declined transactions or security issues.
American Express cards use 4-digit CVV codes. This edge case must be tested to ensure Amex card support.
Expiry date validation prevents accepting expired or malformed cards. Without proper validation, invalid cards could be processed.
Accepting expired cards will result in declined transactions and poor user experience. The expiry check logic needs thorough testing.
Cards expiring in the current month create a boundary condition that could have off-by-one errors in date comparison.
Pricing calculation directly affects revenue. Incorrect calculations could result in undercharging or overcharging customers, leading to revenue loss or legal issues.

testCoverage.summary: ZERO test coverage for critical payment and subscription business logic. This file contains 7 functions (3 exported, 4 internal) handling payment processing, card validation, pricing calculation, subscription management, and feature access control. All functions are completely untested, representing significant risk. Priority testing gaps: Payment processing flow with validation, charging, and subscription upgrade; Card validation edge cases; Pricing calculations; Feature access control for expired subscriptions and unauthorized features; Database error handling; Edge cases for null inputs, malformed data, and boundary dates.

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts file has significant opportunities for improvement across design patterns, type safety, and code organization. Key recommendations: (1) Implement Strategy Pattern for pricing to support multiple pricing models and testing, (2) Replace boolean/exception mixing with Result pattern for consistent error handling, (3) Extract validation logic into small, testable functions, (4) Introduce Repository Pattern to centralize database access, (5) Use branded types for payment data to enforce validation, (6) Centralize tier configuration in a single source of truth, (7) Improve type safety with const assertions and readonly modifiers. These changes would make the code more testable, maintainable, and type-safe while following SOLID principles.

recommendations.description: IMMEDIATE: Remove all PCI-DSS violations by eliminating raw credit card data handling (cardNumber, CVV). Integrate with a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, PayPal, Square) that provides tokenization. Never handle sensitive card data in application code - use payment tokens only.

Replace simulated payment processing with actual payment gateway integration. The current chargeCard function only inserts database records without charging cards, allowing free subscriptions. Integrate real payment API (e.g., Stripe charges API) before production deployment.

Implement database transactions for payment processing. Currently, if chargeCard succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription fails, users are charged without receiving their subscription. Wrap the entire payment flow in a transaction with proper rollback handling.
Add idempotency protection to prevent duplicate charges on network retries or accidental double-clicks. Implement idempotency keys and check for existing payments before processing new ones.

Add comprehensive test coverage for all payment and subscription functions. Currently 0% test coverage on critical business logic. Priority: processPremiumPayment, validatePaymentDetails, calculateSubscriptionPrice, chargeCard, upgradeUserSubscription, hasFeatureAccess, and getUserSubscription with all edge cases.

Add error handling for JSON.parse operations in hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription. Malformed JSON in the database will crash the application. Wrap in try-catch blocks with proper error logging and fallback behavior.

Remove logging of sensitive payment data. The chargeCard function may log full payment objects including card numbers and CVV in error scenarios. Use sanitized logging that only includes non-sensitive identifiers like last 4 digits.

Fix card expiry date validation logic. Current implementation has bugs: doesn't handle month-level expiry correctly, will break in year 2100, and has off-by-one errors. Use proper date comparison at month granularity.

Implement Result/Either pattern for consistent error handling. Currently mixes thrown exceptions and boolean returns, making the API confusing. Return typed success/failure objects with error codes for better client handling.
Replace floating-point money calculations with integer cents to avoid rounding errors. Store all monetary amounts as cents (integers) in the database and convert to dollars only for display.

Extract tier configuration and feature mappings into centralized configuration objects. Currently hardcoded in multiple places, making it difficult to add new tiers or modify features without code changes.

Implement caching for feature access checks. The hasFeatureAccess function performs database queries on every call, which will cause performance issues under high traffic. Add Redis or in-memory caching with appropriate TTL.
Implement Repository Pattern to centralize database access. Create SubscriptionRepository and PaymentRepository classes to encapsulate data access logic, improving testability and maintainability.
Implement branded types for sensitive payment data (CardNumber, CVV, ExpiryDate) to enforce validation at compile time and prevent passing unvalidated strings to payment functions.
Extract validation logic into small, testable functions (isValidCardNumber, isValidCVV, isCardExpired). This improves readability, testability, and makes individual validation rules easier to modify.
